column6:
**What was built:** A toggleable ""Admin Preview Mode"" (cookie-based via Next.js `draftMode()`) that lets admins simulate the full customer experience without affecting production content.

**Features:**

- Toggle button in admin layout (`AdminPreviewToggle`) + amber banner on all public pages when active (`AdminPreviewBanner`)
- Buy buttons intercept payment redirect and instead call `/api/admin/template-access` or `/api/admin/course-access` to grant access directly
- Template download API bypasses payment check in preview mode
- Draft/unpublished templates and courses visible in preview mode
- Profile `/profile` מועדון tab shows full club-member view (`hasActiveSubscription` overridden to `true`)
- `getUserPurchasedTemplates(isAdminPreview)` returns all templates when preview is on
- Dev-only `/api/test/login` endpoint for Playwright E2E auth (disabled in production)
- 5/5 Playwright tests in `e2e/admin-preview-mode.spec.ts`

**Key files:** `src/app/api/admin/preview-mode/route.ts`, `src/app/api/admin/template-access/route.ts`, `src/app/api/admin/course-access/route.ts`, `src/components/admin/AdminPreviewBanner.tsx`, `src/app/admin/components/AdminPreviewToggle.tsx`, `src/app/layout.tsx`, `src/app/admin/layout.tsx`, `src/app/profile/page.tsx`, `src/components/product/ProductPurchaseCard.tsx`, `src/components/public/TemplatesGrid.tsx`""}"

{""kind"": ""source-section"", ""path"": ""/media/endlessblink/data/my-projects/ai-development/freelance/bina-meatzevet-courses/docs/MASTER_PLAN.md"", ""line"": 1944, ""endLine"": 1956, ""text"": ""### ~~TASK-1770: Enroll admin accounts in MFA and enable enforcement (WON'T DO)~~

**Priority**: P0 → closed 2026-04-22
**Depends on**: -
Decision 2026-04-22: **not pursuing Supabase MFA enforcement.** Both real admins (endlessblink@gmail.com, marthastudio.2016@gmail.com) log in exclusively via Google OAuth with Google 2FA enforced at the identity-provider level. Supabase's `aal2` claim is only set by Supabase-managed MFA challenges (TOTP/phone) that happen after the OAuth handshake — it does not reflect Google 2FA. Enforcing Supabase MFA on top of Google 2FA would require admins to carry a second TOTP factor and solve two 6-digit prompts on every login for a marginal security gain (it would only help if Google 2FA itself is bypassed). Google 2FA + the existing `profiles.role='admin'` check is the chosen posture.

Residual risks that now matter more (tracked separately as TASK-1788):

- `resetPasswordForEmail` still works for OAuth-only accounts — inbox compromise → admin takeover.
- `playwright-test@binaclub.com` has `role='admin'` and a real password; if that password leaks, instant admin access.

The middleware AAL gate from TASK-1780 remains in code as dormant insurance — activating it later is a one-line Doppler change if the posture ever changes.
""}"

- `package.json`: `test:e2e` + `test:e2e:ui` now wrap in `doppler run --config dev_test --`. `smoke` left alone.
- `next.config.ts`: CSP `connect-src` / `img-src` / `media-src` and `images.remotePatterns` now derive the Supabase host from `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` (prod fallback). Without this fix the browser fetch from dev_test-bound tests was CSP-blocked. Prod CSP header is byte-identical (env resolves to prod host).

**Step 7 — prod test admin deleted (2026-04-22):**

- `scripts/delete-playwright-test-from-prod.mjs` written with hard safeguards (refuses dev_test, refuses to leave <2 admins, dry-run by default, only deletes the target email).
- Ran dry-run + confirm-delete via `doppler run --config prd --`. Before: 3 admin profiles (endlessblink, marthastudio, playwright-test). After: 2 admin profiles (endlessblink, marthastudio).
- The leaked password `'PlaywrightTest2026!'` in git history no longer authenticates anything anywhere.

**Step 9 — prod smoke (2026-04-22):**

- @smoke 4/4 pass against `https://binaclub.com` (homepage RTL, `/api/health=ok`, `/login` form renders, `/discover` renders).
- Admin API gate verified: `POST /api/admin/preview-mode` and `DELETE /api/admin/templates` both return 401 `נדרשת התחברות` for unauthenticated requests.
- Prod CSP header confirmed resolving to `swdefkgfblgffzdfihnm.supabase.co` (the env-derived path is identical to the previous hardcoded value).

**Pre-existing issue surfaced, not addressed (file separately if pursued):** the `/admin` and `/admin/courses` page-shells return HTTP 200 to unauthenticated requests instead of the middleware redirect to `/`. Data behind them is still RLS-gated and admin APIs return 401, so this is a UX/leak-of-route-existence issue, not an authorization bypass. Worth investigating whether OpenNext on Cloudflare Workers is fully running the Next middleware for these routes.

**Open follow-ups (separate tasks):**

- Investigate the 2 `admin-preview-mode` spec failures (preview-mode API toggle + amber banner) — may need draft-mode cookie handling or a `site_settings.preview_mode_enabled` flag in dev_test fixtures.
- TASK-1790 (proposed in original plan) — split `dev` into its own Supabase project so local development stops touching real customer data.

Why this exists separately from TASK-1788: the immediate fix for the test-admin risk isn't ""rotate the password"" or ""downgrade the role."" It's ""stop authenticating to the production Supabase from tests at all."" Doppler configs already separate `dev_test` (Supabase project `gduotrmsevffbggialsw`) from `dev`/`stg`/`prd` (all share `swdefkgfblgffzdfihnm` — meaning local development today touches real customer data). Vitest already runs through `doppler run --config dev_test`, but Playwright doesn't — `playwright.config.ts` hardcodes the prod Supabase URL and anon key. So the test admin had to be created in prod for Playwright to find it.

**Current dev_test state (probed 2026-04-22):**

- Schema is partially present: `profiles`, `courses` (5 rows), `live_sessions`, `events` tables exist.
- `sections` and `admin_audit_log` are missing (queries returned null) — likely behind on migrations.
- Zero users in `auth.users`; zero rows in `profiles`. The `playwright-test` admin doesn't exist there.
- Doppler `dev_test` config has all required env vars (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY, SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, etc.).

**Migration steps (do in order, each is independently revertable):**

1. **Bring `dev_test` schema current.** From the project root with `dev_test` linked: `supabase link --project-ref gduotrmsevffbggialsw` then `supabase db push` to apply all migrations from `supabase/migrations/`. Verify by re-probing — `sections` and `admin_audit_log` should report row counts (even if zero) instead of null.
2. **Seed the minimum data the existing Playwright specs assume.** Audit `e2e/admin-preview-mode.spec.ts`, `e2e/live-course-recordings.spec.ts`, `e2e/section-surface-migration.spec.ts`, `e2e/purchasing.spec.ts` for hardcoded UUIDs (`LIVE_COURSE_ID`, etc.) and any ""pick the first item from /lives"" assumptions. Seed those rows in `dev_test` via SQL or a one-off seed script. Don't copy production data — fabricate minimal fixtures.
3. **Create the test admin in `dev_test`.** One row in `auth.users` + one row in `profiles` with `role='admin'`. Use a random strong password. Store the password in Doppler `dev_test` as `TEST_USER_PASSWORD`. Email can stay `playwright-test@binaclub.com` for continuity.
4. **Rewrite `playwright.config.ts`** to remove the hardcoded prod Supabase URL/anon key and the hardcoded password. Keep the `process.env.X = X
column3:
fallback` pattern but make the fallback throw a clear error in CI: `if (!process.env.TEST_USER_PASSWORD) throw new Error('Run via doppler run --config dev_test')`. Bake in the `dev_test` Supabase URL/anon key as the new default (those are public values, safe to commit).
5. **Update `package.json` scripts.** Wrap `test:e2e` and `test:e2e:ui` in `doppler run --config dev_test --` so the local dev server they spin up also points at `dev_test` Supabase. Keep `smoke` (which targets a deployed prod URL via SMOKE_BASE_URL) untouched — those specs are read-only and don't need test credentials.
6. **Validate the move.** Run `npm run test:e2e` end-to-end against the local dev server backed by `dev_test`. Fix any spec assumptions that depended on prod data shape.
7. **Delete `playwright-test@binaclub.com` from prod Supabase.** `supabase.auth.admin.deleteUser(...)` via a one-off script using `prd` service-role. Verify with the existing audit script pattern that no admin-role rows in prod profiles remain that aren't endlessblink/marthastudio.
8. **Scrub the password from git history.** `git filter-repo` or BFG to remove `'PlaywrightTest2026!'` from every historical commit of `playwright.config.ts`. This is destructive history rewrite — coordinate with all collaborators (force-push, all clones must re-clone). Optional if step 7 is done and you accept the ""old commit has dead credential"" residual risk.
9. **Smoke check production.** `https://binaclub.com/admin` should still gate the same way (role check on `profiles.role='admin'`); confirm the two real admins (you, Martha) can still log in.

**Bigger architectural concern (out of scope here, file separately if pursued):** dev/stg/prd all sharing one Supabase project means local development edits real customer data. Splitting `dev` into its own Supabase project is a much larger migration (data shape divergence, seed strategy, cron job redirects) and isn't required to land this hardening task. Worth tracking as TASK-1790 if you want to address it.

**Decision points before starting:**

- Are you OK with destructive history rewrite in step 8? (Affects collaborators.)
- Should `dev_test` get periodic data refreshes from prod (sanitized), or stay as fabricated fixtures only? (Latter is simpler, former matches reality better.)

**Priority**: P0
**Depends on**: TASK-1797, TASK-1798, TASK-1799, TASK-1800
Run end-to-end verification before full live rollout: sandbox/real-terminal initial signup, recurring creation row, `MasterRecurring` report, `DetailRecurring` success/failure capture where possible, user self-cancel, and profile state. Then flip only the club subscription plan to `payment_provider='cardcom'`, monitor `cardcom_webhook_events`, `cardcom_transactions`, `payments`, and access state before rolling out anything else.

**Progress (2026-04-27):** Fixed Cardcom webhook body parsing for E2E recurring readiness. The route now reads the request body once and supports JSON plus Cardcom name-value/form-encoded reports, including callbacks that arrive without a reliable content type. Added focused tests for JSON, form-encoded `DetailRecurring`, and bare name-value `MasterRecurring` parsing.

**Progress (2026-04-27):** E2E preflight passed for configured secrets and applied Cardcom tables. Flipped the inactive `student-club` subscription plan to `payment_provider='cardcom'` as an isolated test target and created a confirmed E2E test user. Deployed checkout smoke reached the route but Cardcom rejected LowProfile creation with `ResponseCode=5047` because invoice lines were missing; fixed the checkout payload to include a `Document.Products` line item. Direct LowProfile verification against Cardcom now returns `ResponseCode=0` and a hosted payment URL. No payment was completed yet, so no webhook, transaction, subscription, recurring, or payment rows are expected for the E2E user.

**Progress (2026-04-27):** Completed a real 1 ILS Cardcom charge against an inactive `Cardcom E2E 1 ILS` plan. `GetLpResult` confirmed transaction `245971636`, token creation, document `1`, and amount `1`. Cardcom did not automatically call our webhook, so replayed the callback manually; production fetched GetLpResult but skipped activation because real successful `TokenInfo` omits `ResponseCode`. Fixed `isGetLpResultSuccess()` to treat missing token response as success, then manually mirrored the paid result: `cardcom_transactions` succeeded, `payments` completed, `subscriptions` active through 2026-05-27, and `RecurringPayment.aspx` created Hora'at Keva with `AccountId=1000`, `RecurringId=20000`. Cancellation was tested against Cardcom and returned `ResponseCode=0`; local recurring row is `cancelled` while subscription access remains active through paid expiry.

**Progress (2026-04-27, 12:57 — save point for next session):** Deploy is live and healthy. Shipped: (1) checkout invoice line fix, (2) real `TokenInfo.ResponseCode` handling, (3) JSON / form / name-value webhook parsing. Verified: production homepage 200, `/api/health` `{""status"":""ok""}`. Deployed `POST /api/cardcom/checkout` now creates real hosted payment URLs against Cardcom. Latest test URL generated through `https://binaclub.com/api/cardcom/checkout` (1 ILS): `https://secure.cardcom.solutions/EA/LPC6/188053/3034fa54-8e5a-4bad-b8b1-54c7e8737b23?t=24`.

**Progress (2026-07-07):** Added a Cardcom renewal audit and guarded repair lane. Production read-only audit classified 16 recurring rows: 2 healthy, 3 cancelled, and 11 active-but-overdue rows where `MasterRecurring` remains active with `NumOfPaymentsAlreadyCharged=0`, no `DetailRecurring` webhook, no `subscription_renewal` transaction, and no matching Cardcom financial row. Added `/api/admin/cardcom/renewal-audit`, `/admin/billing` visibility, dry-run repair classification, and an exact confirmation gate (`CHARGE <RecurringId>`) before any retroactive token charge can run. Focused renewal/Cardcom/profile tests passed.

**Progress (2026-07-07):** Root cause narrowed further: the app-managed token renewal route already existed at `/api/cron/cardcom-renew`, but the production Worker scheduled handler was not calling it. Wired the Worker cron to call the route, kept it safe-by-default behind `CARDCOM_RENEW_CRON_ENABLED=true`, and changed late-renewal expiry calculation to extend from the renewal run time instead of repeatedly catching up from an old expired date. Successful cron renewals now write `return_value=sub:<subscriptionId>` so the renewal audit can recognize them. Retroactive charges for the 11 overdue rows remain a deliberate admin repair action, not an automatic cron side effect.

**Progress (2026-07-20):** Closed the duplicate-renewal incident end to end. Cardcom is the sole authority for provider-managed orders; the app token cron now refuses those rows even if enabled. Subscription checkout blocks a second live order for the same billing family even when access already expired, completed stale checkouts are automatically refunded, provider callbacks disable superseded orders instead of extending old access, the audit detects live duplicates independent of subscription access status, and admin delete/reset paths fail closed unless every provider order is disabled. Production repair refunded the duplicate renewal, retired the stale order, restored complimentary access for the missed-renewal customer through August 1, moved her provider billing date to August 1, and verified zero overdue or duplicate rows.

**Progress (2026-07-20, hardening):** Independent review expanded the guard from exact plan IDs to canonical billing families, added an atomic short-lived checkout lock across old/new club prices, made stale paid checkouts automatically refund with a replay-safe zero-balance ledger, preserved superseded-order quarantine through provider callbacks, added automatic cancellation retry without enabling token charging, persisted each provider cancellation before multi-order cleanup continues, and made admin test reset atomic. Production migrations 186–187 were dry-run, applied, and verified; old ₪89 and current ₪99 plans now share `general_club`, while the student club remains independent.

**Next steps (resume here):**

1. User pays 1 ILS via the Cardcom URL above — _do not_ manually cancel after payment.
2. Verify the deployed webhook fires: rows in `cardcom_webhook_events`, `cardcom_transactions`, `payments`, `subscriptions` (active through ~2026-05-27), and `cardcom_recurring_plans` (Hora'at Keva via `RecurringPayment.aspx`).
3. Log in as the E2E test user at `/profile`, click cancel, and verify Cardcom disables the recurring order while `/club` access stays active until paid `expires_at`.
4. **Open issue (2026-04-27 12:57):** user reports the latest hosted checkout URL returns ""page failed to load"" in browser — investigate before retrying the pay step (URL may have already been consumed/expired by Cardcom, or LowProfile guid was issued for a single visit).
""}"

**Why**: Admins need one zero-downtime, testable customer/contact lifecycle from first email lead through signup, free-live registration, automated emails, club/course purchase, cancellation, recording release, and weekly content updates.

**Priority**: P0
**Why**: The UUID-derived link was still too long, and WhatsApp retained a text-only cached preview instead of showing the updated event artwork.

**Scope** — let admins set a short English event alias such as `ai-live`; resolve both aliases and existing UUID-derived links; give new lives a compact editable default; and cache versioned social artwork at the edge so WhatsApp can retrieve the current cover reliably.

**Verify** — alias normalization and compatibility tests; admin link-field tests; authenticated mobile editor review; normal-browser and WhatsApp-crawler route checks; generated-image visual review; full PR checks; exact production deploy and health; and a fresh WhatsApp share using the new alias.

**2026-07-19** — Reopened after the real WhatsApp composer still produced a generic text-only card. Automated metadata and image checks were insufficient; completion now requires the compact alias to put its social tags before all application scripts and a fresh preview to appear in WhatsApp itself.

**2026-07-20** — A real WhatsApp preview exposed that Satori was painting each Hebrew line in left-to-right word order. The social-image helper now converts every wrapped line to visual RTL order, with focused regression coverage and a new image/link cache identity; completion still requires production deployment and a fresh WhatsApp screenshot.

**2026-07-20** — The `share7` WhatsApp screenshot proved that reversing words alone still mirrored Hebrew letters because Satori does not support RTL typography. The replacement conversion now reverses Hebrew grapheme clusters as well as visual runs, preserves English phrases, is compared against a browser-native RTL reference, and advances to `preview5/share8`; the task remains open for a fresh WhatsApp screenshot.

**2026-07-20** — The production `share8` PNG was correct, but WhatsApp continued showing the prior artwork because both cache identities only changed query strings. The next fix uses new pathnames for the compact page (`preview6`) and social image (`share9`) so the scraper cannot collapse them onto the old cached paths; regression coverage now locks the path-based identities.

**2026-07-20** — The new pathname format produced a reliable WhatsApp preview, but its generated thumbnail duplicated the card copy at an unreadably small size. The next artwork revision (`preview7/share10`) removes all embedded text and uses only the CMS background and presenter images; prior pathname and query links remain valid redirects.

**2026-07-20** — Production visual verification approved the image-only composition, then the focused production browser regression caught a 496 KB payload above the existing 300 KB crawler budget. The follow-up `preview8/share11` identity retains the background and sharp portrait, gently softens only the background, and publishes accurate 560×294 metadata without weakening the payload guard.

**2026-07-20** — The real WhatsApp composer confirmed the image-only card and exposed one final thumbnail-safe-area issue: WhatsApp center-crops the 1.9:1 artwork and clipped the presenter at the right edge. The `preview9/share12` revision moves the portrait inward while preserving the approved artwork, payload budget, and every prior redirect.

**2026-07-21** — After the uncropped WhatsApp proof, the approved default was refined for stronger small-card composition: the presenter is centered and enlarged to occupy approximately half of WhatsApp's visible thumbnail width. The shared `preview10/share13` renderer applies this to current and future lives, while earlier link versions remain compatible.

**2026-07-21** — The centered circular portrait did not match the intended “half the image” direction. The `preview11/share14` revision replaces it with a clean vertical split: the cover fills the left half and the presenter fills the full-height right half without a circle; when either image is absent, the available image fills the whole preview. Earlier compact links remain compatible.

**2026-07-21** — Exact production inspection found that the legacy CMS cover already contained a miniature presenter and caption, duplicating Nitzan inside the new split. The `preview12/share15` follow-up crops that legacy composite to its clean architectural region while leaving ordinary future cover images untouched.

**2026-07-21** — The clean production split was visually correct but its detailed PNG reached 328 KB, above the established 300 KB WhatsApp retrieval budget. The `preview13/share16` revision lightly softens only the cropped legacy architecture panel to reduce payload while preserving the sharp full-height presenter and the 50/50 composition.

**2026-07-21 — DONE** — The user accepted the final split preview. All five PR checks and the guarded full production deploy passed; production health is OK, legacy compact links still resolve, and the visually verified 560×294 WhatsApp artwork is 246,090 bytes with a clean architectural half and a sharp full-height presenter.

{""kind"": ""source-section"", ""path"": ""/media/endlessblink/data/my-projects/ai-development/freelance/bina-meatzevet-courses/docs/MASTER_PLAN.md"", ""line"": 119, ""endLine"": 187, ""text"": ""### TASK-1966: Rebuild the campaign communication workspace with E2E safety (IN PROGRESS)

**Priority**: P0
**Why**: The prior Email Center work improved isolated safeguards but still leaves campaign identity, audience purpose, link truth, approval snapshots, and the operator path too ambiguous for a safe production send.

**Scope** — implement the documented requirements in `docs/plans/communication-workspace-prd.md`: stable campaign URLs and versions, immutable audience/link snapshots, explicit promotional versus event-subscriber rules, canonical Nitzan recording resolution, guided RTL workspace, approval invalidation, idempotent delivery/recovery, audit history, visual/a11y E2E coverage, and production publish evidence without sending a real audience.

**Verify** — unit/integration/policy/link/delivery tests, authenticated headed desktop/mobile RTL screenshots, design detector and security review, CI checks, migration verification, production route/link/audience smoke, and an honest release report.

**Progress 2026-09-24** — Prepared `docs/plans/internal-scheduled-email-test-plan.md` as a non-executing internal test plan. The schedule-sensitive approval evidence hash and immutable approval version snapshot now include `scheduled_for`; admin scheduling now converts Israel local time explicitly; automatic registration/event-link, admin registration/purchase notifications, and payment/access lifecycle sends now carry deterministic Resend idempotency keys; focused campaign/lifecycle tests, typecheck, lint, and whitespace checks pass. No production campaign, provider mutation, or customer email was performed; authorization and deployed/browser/provider/inbox proof remain open.

**Progress 2026-08-09** — created the PRD, unknowns/decision register, risk register, state model, decision tables, test matrix, and migration foundation; locked and fixed the canonical recording-link regression; added HTTPS/public redirect and Canva link validation, stable campaign identity helpers, dashboard-first RTL coverage, and transactional approval evidence for version/audience/links/audit/batches. Focused unit/action tests, typecheck, detector, and isolated headed desktop/mobile E2E pass. Read-only production health returned `ok` and the protected campaign route returned `307`; exact production commit, migration, audience counts, Nitzan identity, and destination proof remain OPEN. The full Vitest run is not green because the existing production-data audit reports a published live missing its image.
**Production proof update 2026-08-10** — rebuilt the proof branch from the latest `origin/main` to remove unrelated stale deletions. The guarded read-only audit confirms 191 registrations, 112 consented registrations, 12 suppressions, 0 workspace versions/links, and no real send; the selected event is published in data but its canonical URL returns 404, and authenticated production credentials remain unavailable.
**Production destination fix 2026-08-10** — generated event rows now resolve their linked course and route to the correct public `/lives`, `/courses`, or `/events` destination. The read-only production audit returned HTTP 200 for the selected live destination; targeted campaign tests and typecheck pass, with authenticated production access still unverified.
**Authenticated review findings 2026-08-10** — the extension-attached headed browser opened the stable production campaign URL and verified the consent-only audience at 150 eligible of 153, with approval and test-send disabled until a test recipient is selected. It also found a stale broad-audience label and three legacy course links returning 404; commits `85578fbc` and `1521e5d0` correct the summary source and persist canonical enriched URLs, pending deployment and re-verification.
**Post-deploy proof 2026-08-10** — merge commit `5b1e1202` deployed successfully in workflow `31411293146` (worker version `fa67f2ba-c87d-4e3a-b5f3-d8ceec3770ae`); `/api/health` returned `ok`. The fresh production audit at `2026-08-10T17:04:15.508Z` reports `recording_segment: course_consent`, canonical recording/live/course links all HTTP 200, and `realSendPerformed: false`.
**Stable-route proof 2026-08-10** — PR `672` merged as `894b328b` and deployed successfully in workflow `31413966291`; `/api/health` returned `ok` at `2026-08-10T17:32:33.307Z`. The authenticated visible browser loaded the campaign ID route with the campaign heading and RTL workspace; the extension relay disconnected before a continuous interaction sequence, so no send or approval action is claimed.
**Parallel gap audit 2026-08-12** — Four read-only audits (production, campaign safety, email security, and CI/CD) agree that this task remains OPEN and must not enable a real audience send. Highest-priority blockers are: saved-campaign URL state is hydrated server-side but not kept in sync through browser navigation/refresh; approval and audience evidence are not fully immutable or atomic; lifecycle templates can become approved without persisted render/test proof; campaign batches still use the Resend SDK path instead of the worker-safe direct sender; test-send recipients include hardcoded personal addresses; URL/link validation is not a hard approval gate; archived events can leave scheduled campaigns deliverable; exact Nitzan/David event identity needs an explicit regression; and production deployment authority is split between GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Builds, and an unpromoted VPS runner. The nightly “production” audit currently runs against `dev_test`; migration drift is warn-open; and the Cloudflare path lacks parity for secret reconciliation, smoke, migration gating, and rollback.

**Full-path execution plan 2026-08-12** — This is the authoritative sequence for the remaining work. Independent audits may run in parallel only with disjoint read-only scopes; implementation and release remain serialized at each gate.

1. **Evidence baseline** — inventory the current production commit, deployed worker version, migration state, campaign routes, event/course identity, consent fields, suppression sources, provider configuration, and current email-render output. Gate: every claim has a command/query/screenshot artifact; no send and no migration application.
2. **Identity and lifecycle safety** — finish browser URL hydration/refresh, exact campaign-version restoration, archive/delete semantics, stale approval invalidation, archived-event test/approve/send blocks, and atomic audience/approval evidence. Gate: route/action integration tests prove the same approved snapshot is the only deliverable snapshot.
3. **Audience and Nitzan correctness** — resolve promotional consent versus event subscription from authoritative production data, confirm the exact Nitzan live and recording destination, validate suppression/exclusion and count reconciliation, and add data-backed regression fixtures. Gate: UI summary, stored snapshot, and send-time selection agree; no campaign is eligible while any identity or count is unresolved.
4. **Link and template integrity** — validate every stored and rendered-email destination, final URL/redirect chain, Canva reachability, recording canonicalization, template render hashes, and content-driven course/live/social preview fields. Gate: approval is impossible with any missing, stale, dead, ambiguous, or unproven link/render artifact.
5. **Operator UX and email design** — restore the four-stage guided RTL flow without duplicated legacy surfaces, simplify dashboard filtering/archive controls, reduce scroll, and redesign the actual rendered email with intentional breathing room and right-aligned RTL cards. Gate: Impeccable + Bina design + RTL/accessibility review, headed desktop/mobile screenshots, and manual interaction evidence for every changed surface.
6. **Delivery reliability** — use the direct provider-safe sender for all campaign paths, enforce idempotency per version/recipient, safe transient retry, suppression at enqueue/send, clear partial failures, audit linkage, unsubscribe headers, and no silent fallback. Gate: provider-mock and recipient-level tests plus a no-send test configuration; only internal allowlisted test mail may be sent.
7. **CI/CD and production parity** — finish the VPS runner path or document the exact remaining external credential gate, serialize deploy triggers, add secret/config checks, migration dry-run/apply verification, build/liveness/smoke/rollback/log gates, and remove paid GitHub-hosted execution from the production path if the VPS path proves equivalent. Gate: one exact commit, one traceable deploy, one healthy rollback-capable release; no duplicate dispatches.
8. **Release proof** — run focused unit/integration/policy/link/delivery tests, full typecheck/build in the supported lane, authenticated headed RTL visual E2E, accessibility checks, production health, protected campaign route, stable URL restoration, destination checks, and audience reconciliation. Gate: honest release report lists PASS, UNVERIFIED, and BLOCKED separately; no real Nitzan send until every send gate is green.

**Parallel specialist routing** — when capacity is available, assign separate read-only lanes to: (A) campaign data/consent/Nitzan identity, (B) visual/email/a11y E2E, (C) VPS/Cloudflare/Doppler release parity, and (D) delivery/security/retry audit. Each lane must return evidence and exact next actions, never mutate production or send mail. Current delegation capacity is not available: the bridge reports stale pending audits assigned to an offline agent; this is recorded as an orchestration issue, not a reason to skip any gate.

**Issue-flush checklist** — before release, explicitly re-check: stable URL after direct load/browser navigation/refresh; old noisy dashboard surfaces removed; template preview/edit/create/update/delete; event future/past/type/archive filters and thumbnails; course-driven email content with manual override; correct “X of Y” audience counts; promotional consent never labeled as all registrants; Nitzan recording destination; final rendered-email links; approval invalidation after every material edit; archived campaigns/events blocked at test/approve/send; direct sender/idempotency/retry/partial failure/audit; empty/loading/error/disabled/permission states; RTL desktop/mobile clipping/focus/contrast; migration authority; exact deployed commit; production smoke; and no real send during testing.
**Execution order after audit** — First finish and verify the current stable-URL hydration PR without claiming send readiness. Next create separate, bounded safety slices: authoritative release-path decision and fail-closed CI/CD gates; server-side immutable campaign/version/audience/link/test/approval evidence with transactional approval; exact audience and event/link resolution tests; worker-safe idempotent delivery plus restricted test allowlist; lifecycle template render/test proof; archive/delete/recovery semantics; then authenticated headed desktop/mobile RTL proof and production route/link/health verification. No real campaign send is permitted until every slice has passing tests and production evidence.
**Subagent plan synthesis 2026-08-12** — The full path is now tracked as seven gates: (1) consolidate requirements and release authority; (2) close campaign URL, test-recipient, and direct-provider delivery safety; (3) make audience, consent, canonical links, template provenance, and approval evidence immutable; (4) restore the guided RTL dashboard and content-driven email preview with explicit empty/loading/error/disabled states; (5) prove VPS CI/CD isolation, serialized triggers, logs, notifications, rollback, and staging parity; (6) run unit/integration/policy/link/delivery, accessibility, headed desktop/mobile RTL, and rendered-email verification; (7) deploy one exact commit and re-run authenticated production route, audience, link, health, and no-send smoke checks. Each gate must record evidence or remain OPEN; a green build, health endpoint, screenshot, or deploy alone cannot advance it.
**Specialist audit refresh 2026-08-12** — Six occupied agent reviews were used where independent work was safe; two additional read-only end-to-end audits were completed and their findings merged here. The current unresolved issue list is: (a) template records persist structured content but no rendered HTML/text hash or preview evidence; (b) production and `dev_test` migration authority/configuration are not both proven; (c) the real Nitzan recording/event identity still needs a data-backed regression, not a fixture-only check; (d) canonical link checks still need final-destination assertions and rendered-email inventory verification; (e) archived event/campaign behavior needs a send-time guard; (f) approval/audience evidence needs an integration-level atomicity test; (g) production authenticated proof and exact deployed commit remain OPEN; and (h) the VPS runner queue is a throughput constraint, not evidence that deployment is safe. No sub-agent may mutate production data, send mail, apply migrations, or publish without an explicit parent-agent gate and recorded evidence.
**Archive and identity evidence 2026-08-12** — Campaign test-send and approval actions now fail closed before recipient loading/provider delivery/approval RPC when their source event is archived; focused action and delivery tests pass `47/47`, typecheck passes, and commit `9de4b925` is pushed. Fresh strict read-only production audits confirm the exact Nitzan event and counts, but keep the broad placeholder draft and three-404-link draft blocked; no production send or data mutation occurred.
**Rendered-link gate 2026-08-12** — The shared renderer now exposes the final HTTP link inventory from emitted email HTML. Test-send and approval validate that inventory before provider delivery or atomic approval, include the validated rendered links in evidence hashing, and block inline dead links; focused render/action tests pass `55/55`, typecheck passes, and commit `fd2c1ef3` is pushed.
**Send-time archive gate 2026-08-12** — Batch delivery now loads `archived_at` and, when archiving occurs after approval, skips queued recipients, completes the batch without provider delivery, and cancels the campaign explicitly. Focused delivery tests pass `12/12`, typecheck passes, and the local diff is clean; production deployment/re-verification remain open.
**Approval atomicity gate 2026-08-12** — The migration contract now locks the evidence order: audience snapshot and links are inserted and link validity is checked before approval/batch creation and audit rows. The contract suite passes `12/12`; a real `dev_test` rollback exercise remains required before this is treated as database integration proof.
**Database rollback proof 2026-08-12** — The opt-in integration test `campaign-workspace.integration.test.ts` passed against isolated `dev_test`: an invalid link rejected approval and left no version, snapshot, link, approval, batch, or recipient artifacts; the campaign stayed `draft`, no provider was called, and production was refused by an explicit URL guard. The default suite does not enable this mutating test.
**Browser renderer regression proof 2026-08-12** — The headed campaign visual gate caught a `node:crypto` client-bundle failure that prevented hydration and made fixture cleanup return HTTP 500. The renderer now uses Web Crypto SHA-256; focused render/template/content tests pass `38/38`, and desktop/mobile headed visual tests pass `2/2`. Production redeploy and re-verification remain open.
**Production identity expectation proof 2026-08-12** — The read-only production audit now fails closed when expected event title or recording URL differs. The strict Nitzan check matched event `ed9a87ff-4acd-424f-8015-64d40ad7008d`, title, YouTube recording, canonical live HTTP 200, counts `191/112/12`, and `realSendPerformed: false`; this is not send authorization.
**Stable URL hydration proof 2026-08-12** — A new direct-load assertion exposed that the bare campaign URL opened the dashboard instead of the guided flow. Hydration now defaults canonical campaign URLs to `surface=send&tab=audience` while preserving explicit query state; headed desktop/mobile RTL visual cases pass `2/2`. Production route re-verification remains open.

column2:
**Priority**: P1
**Files**: `src/lib/utils.ts`, `src/app/editor/[id]/page.tsx`, `src/components/editor/versions-canvas.tsx`, `CLAUDE.md`

**Problems**:
1. Long titles got horizontally clipped in the editor because `<input>` can't wrap text
2. Mixed Hebrew/English titles rendered LTR under `dir=""auto""` (first strong char wins), despite containing Hebrew
3. Versions canvas had `dir=""rtl""` hardcoded on all user-content containers, forcing English posts to render RTL with punctuation on the wrong side
4. Root node card was oversized (320×350) and dumped full post content
5. Borders and placeholder outlines were too faint to see on dark background

**Fixes**:
- Added `dirFor(text)` helper in `src/lib/utils.ts` — returns `""rtl""` if Hebrew chars (U+0590–U+05FF) appear anywhere, else `""ltr""`. Rule: any Hebrew → RTL
- Editor title: converted `<input>` to auto-growing `<textarea>` with `dir={dirFor(title)}` so long titles wrap cleanly in the correct direction
- Focus-mode title: same `dirFor(title)` treatment
- Versions canvas: replaced all `dir=""rtl""` on user-content elements with `dir={dirFor(...)}` (root title, root body, version body, edit textarea, streaming text, static version text). Kept `dir=""rtl""` on UI chrome (Hebrew buttons, labels, placeholder text)
- Root node: 320×350 → 280×180, body uses `line-clamp-3` instead of full content, title uses `line-clamp-2` instead of `truncate`
- Borders bumped from `#2A2A2A` → `#3A3A3A` (nodes) and `#444444` (placeholder dashed)
- Added verification rule at top of `CLAUDE.md` — all UI fixes must be visually verified via Playwright CLI screenshot before being claimed as done
""}

column1: {""kind"": ""source-section"", ""path"": ""/media/endlessblink/data/my-projects/ai-development/content-creation/inner-dialouge/MASTER_PLAN.md"", ""line"": 1071, ""endLine"": 1108, ""text"": ""### FEATURE-087: Canvas tab view for social version management\n**Status**: ✅ DONE (2026-04-11)
column2:
**Priority**: P1  
**Depends on**: —

Canvas-based version management for social media adaptations of posts. Two tabs at the top of the editor: ""עריכה"" (Edit) and ""גרסאות"" (Versions). The Versions tab shows a full React Flow canvas with:

- **Root node**: Original post (title + content preview)
- **Child nodes**: Platform-specific versions (WhatsApp, LinkedIn, Facebook, X)
- **Branching**: Multiple versions per platform, re-improve from any version
- **Click to edit**: Clicking a node loads that version in the editor tab for deep editing
- **Auto-layout**: dagre/elkjs tree layout, with manual drag override
- **Zoom/pan**: Built-in React Flow controls + minimap
- **Persistence**: Canvas state (node positions, viewport) saved per-post in DB
- **Each post has its own graph view**

**Tech**: `@xyflow/react` (React Flow), `dagre` for auto-layout

**Already built (backend)**:
- `segmentVersions` schema with `parentVersionId`, `updatedAt` columns
- CRUD API routes: GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE at `/api/posts/[id]/segment-versions`
- `useVersionGraph` hook with social mode (fetches all, filters by `social-*` commands)
- Social versions graph component (current sidebar version, to be replaced by canvas)

**Completed (2026-04-11)**:
- Installed `@xyflow/react` + `dagre` + `@types/dagre`
- Tab UI in editor page (עריכה / גרסאות) with localStorage persistence
- `versions-canvas.tsx`: React Flow canvas with dagre auto-layout (TB), 3 custom node types
- RootNode: full post content, word count, ""Generate All"" button
- VersionNode: platform icon, char count badge, inline edit, copy/regenerate/delete, streaming
- PlaceholderNode: dashed outline, click-to-generate for missing platforms
- Nodes are draggable and resizable (NodeResizer with purple handles)
- Scroll inside nodes works (nowheel class)
- MiniMap + Controls + dark theme
- Delete confirmation dialog
- Removed old sidebar social-versions-graph, social-versions, version-overlay (dead code)
- 3 e2e tests: canvas render, drag, resize
- `contentText` initialized from post data on load (fixes empty content on versions tab)
""}

While the user types in the Tiptap editor, surrounding chrome (sidebar, header, side-notes, chat-sidebar, editor top bar) fades to 0.4 opacity after ~1.2s. Snaps back on mouse-move, focus-out, or ~2s typing pause. Implementation via `body[data-chrome-faded=""1""]` attribute + `:where(...)` CSS selector to avoid Context plumbing. Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`. Piggybacks Tiptap's existing `onUpdate` rather than adding a second listener.

Implemented with `useTypingState()`, `data-chrome-fade-target` markers on editor chrome/sidebar/chat surfaces, reduced-motion CSS, and Playwright coverage in `e2e/editor-ai-regression.spec.ts`.
""}"

Capture drafts for new tool launches should default to a concise product-post format: new tool, distinctive features, and market fit. The current flow improved fact coverage but still produced drafts that were too long, generic, and sometimes convoluted in comparison sentences.

Implemented by tightening the capture draft system prompt around short feature-first tool posts, requiring exactly 3 feature details before comparisons, preferring simple `מול Remotion:` comparison lines, and rejecting accidental faux-personal phrasing such as `בעיניי`. Added focused prompt regressions for these constraints. Evaluated Grok for cheap synthesis: there is no text Grok/xAI provider in the app, while OpenRouter already supports cheap alternate synthesis models through the existing provider path, so no separate provider/settings surface was added.

Acceptance criteria:
- Default tool-launch posts stay short, roughly 120-160 Hebrew words unless requested otherwise.
- Use 3 concrete distinctive features before any market comparison.
- Comparisons are simple lines such as `מול Remotion: ...`, not multi-clause sentences.
- Avoid generic framing like ""וידאו שאפשר לערוך כמו דף web"" unless backed by specific features.
- Reject accidental first-person phrasing like `בעיניי` unless explicitly requested.
- Evaluate adding Grok as a cheap synthesis provider for already-collected launch/X context.
""}"

Add an AI action that converts an existing regular post into a structured screenplay. The AI reads the full post body and maps each paragraph to a screenplay semantic role (scene heading, action/description, character, dialogue, parenthetical, transition), the post `type` flips to `screenplay`, and the body re-renders with screenplay fonts/layout. The conversion is non-destructive: a preview is shown and the user confirms before the canonical text is replaced.

Implemented a ""המר לתסריט"" toolbar button (shown only for non-screenplay posts) that calls a dedicated `/api/ai/screenplay-convert` endpoint. The endpoint prompts the active AI provider to return a strict JSON array of `{type, text}` screenplay elements, validated against the semantic node types. The result is shown in a preview dialog rendered with screenplay styling; on accept, the current post is snapshotted as a recoverable version, the body is replaced with semantic screenplay Tiptap nodes, and `type` flips to `screenplay`. The editor key is keyed on `type` so it remounts with screenplay nodes/layout/outline/canvas. Verified end-to-end in the browser (Playwright) and against the live Claude CLI provider.

Acceptance criteria:
- A regular post exposes a ""convert to screenplay"" AI action.
- AI classifies each block as scene heading, action/description, character, dialogue, parenthetical, or transition, and emits valid semantic screenplay Tiptap JSON.
- On accept, the post `type` becomes `screenplay` and the editor switches to screenplay layout/fonts.
- Conversion is non-destructive: a preview is shown and the user confirms before the body is replaced; original is recoverable via versions/undo.
- Hebrew RTL screenplay layout is preserved (per existing screenplay conventions).
- The action is hidden for posts already typed `screenplay`.
""}

Harden the writing workspace against stale sidebar/project state while adding publishing QA tools that keep AI output conservative and inspectable.

Implemented a shared browser app-event layer so post/project create, update, delete, restore, conversion, and version actions keep sidebar, project counts, and project post lists in sync without a full reload. The sidebar now supports scoped document views, recent/unassigned/project filters, safer project-aware post creation, and better mixed-direction titles. Quality checks can highlight the exact editor range, fact checks use web research sources through a dedicated command, and social WhatsApp output now preserves original wording and paragraph spacing more conservatively.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sidebar/project lists update immediately after post and project mutations.
- Moving, creating, deleting, restoring, converting, or version-restoring a post does not leave stale sidebar/project state.
- Sidebar scopes support all documents, recent documents, unassigned posts, and project-specific views.
- Quality-check findings can highlight and scroll to the affected editor text.
- Fact-check command returns bounded sourced JSON issues from web research context.
- WhatsApp social versions preserve source wording, opening lines, and paragraph spacing unless a platform constraint requires a change.

column2:
**Priority**: P1
**Files**: `src/lib/bidi.ts`, `src/components/editor/editor.tsx`, `src/components/editor/versions-canvas.tsx`, `src/app/globals.css`, `e2e/editor-ai-regression.spec.ts`

Mixed Hebrew/English writing still broke around English tool names when Hebrew prefixes, conjunctions, or punctuation touched the Latin run. Cases like `ה-AI`, `AI וכתיבה`, `AI-ווידאו`, `ו-Freepik`, and `Kling.` need the English token isolated LTR while the Hebrew marks and punctuation stay in the surrounding RTL sentence flow.

Implemented a shared bidi tokenizer for English runs and reused it in both the Tiptap editor decorations and social versions canvas renderer. The tokenizer keeps hyphens inside an LTR run only when they connect Latin/number tokens, leaving Hebrew prefixes/suffixes and punctuation outside the isolate. Added focused Playwright regression coverage for these mixed-boundary cases.

Acceptance criteria:
- Hebrew/mixed blocks remain RTL and right-aligned.
- English runs are isolated without swallowing Hebrew prefixes such as `ה-` or `ו-`.
- Hebrew text immediately after `AI`, including `AI ו...` and `AI-ו...`, remains outside the LTR isolate.
- Sentence punctuation after English tool names stays in the surrounding RTL flow.
- Editor and version-card rendering share the same bidi tokenizer.""}"

**Priority:** P1
**Status:** ✅ DONE (2026-07-29). Data model, frame resolution, preview rendering,
timeline censor lane, draw-on-preview creation, and the user-facing styled export all
work and are covered, including a real pixelated mosaic in exported files. Cut ranges
(slice 7) are done, and a censor can now follow moving content — either from tracking
or from hand-placed positions — in the preview and in both export backends. Confirmed
on a real recording by the user.

Four defects were found by testing exported pixels rather than filter graphs, and all
are guarded by tests that were verified to fail without their fix:

- a censor placed after a cut fired a second late, showing what it was meant to hide;
- solid-colour censors froze in place while appearing to follow, because the box
  filter evaluates its geometry once and has no per-frame option;
- following a censor longer than a few minutes exhausted memory (1.2GB retained,
  2.4GB peak) because every analysed frame was collected before any was matched;
- a censor deleted while an analysis was running came back, because the analysis
  wrote back the document it had captured when it started.

**Open follow-up:** on one real recording a second censor lost its target and held
position. Not reproduced — a synthetic dark, low-contrast sliding target tracks
correctly — and it now reports honestly when that happens instead of claiming to
follow. Needs the actual footage to tune against. Separately, zoom timing appears to
have the same cut/trim flaw the censor gates had, and is untouched.
""}

Noam decided on 2026-09-30 to release Rough Cut, including the Claude graphics tool, for free under AGPL. No paid split, no licence
key, no gated graphics. This replaces the 29.09 ""free core plus paid graphics ($29 early-bird, then $49)"" bundle. Full reasoning, how

- Why: Open Edit (VEED, Apache-2.0, 1,391 stars two months after launch) makes prompt-made motion graphics free through coding agents;
  three free recorders already have 23k to 40k stars; the goal is reach and reputation that feeds Noam's freelance search.
- Charge later, from data, 4 to 6 weeks after launch (about mid November 2026): Pro add-ons built after launch, convenience builds,
  a company licence, sponsors and services. The README must say a paid Pro may come later for new features. If outside contributions
  are accepted, contributors sign an agreement so relicensing stays possible.
- The standout to build on: Claude graphics as editable layers on the user's own recording, transparent overlay export, Linux-first.
""}"

column1: {""kind"": ""source-section"", ""path"": ""/media/endlessblink/data/my-projects/ai-development/web-dev/bina-ve-ze/MASTER_PLAN.md"", ""line"": 825, ""endLine"": 834, ""text"": ""#### T-029 — Folder interaction depth\n- **Type:** FEATURE
column3:
**Status:** TODO
- **File:** `src/pages/PersonalSite.tsx`
- **Problem:** Today a folder just toggles a sticky-note preview. A desktop metaphor that doesn't *open* wastes the affordance — users expect contents, not a description card.
- **Options to pick from (decide during build):**
  1. **In-place ""spread""** — folder opens and fans out 3–6 thumbnails of inner items right above it (best for spatial feel, keeps user on the desktop).
  2. **Window** — folder opens a draggable Finder-style window listing items (heavier, more authentic, more code).
  3. **Route push** — folder navigates to a sub-page (`/videos`, `/guides`, etc.) — simplest, but breaks the spatial illusion.

column1: {""kind"": ""source-section"", ""path"": ""/media/endlessblink/data/my-projects/ai-development/web-dev/bina-ve-ze/MASTER_PLAN.md"", ""line"": 698, ""endLine"": 737, ""text"": ""### T-057 — Homepage motion journey brief\n- **Type:** TASK
column3:
**Status:** DONE
- **Owner:** current design/dev lane
- **Files:** `MASTER_PLAN.md`, `DESIGN.md`
- **Result:** The existing desktop should become the destination of an intro, not the entire opening scene.
- **Motion storyboard:**
  1. **Invitation:** a clear Hebrew opening line and one strong action introduce the AI studio.
  2. **Materialization:** a memorable AI/OS object or command-window artifact animates in the first viewport.
  3. **Transition:** the object settles into the desktop; windows, shortcuts, and dock arrive from that moment.
  4. **Handoff:** the existing OS desktop becomes usable after the intro.
  5. **Explore:** hover, focus, drag, workspace switching, and dock usage keep the desktop responsive.
- **Signature interactions for T-058:**
  - **Animated intro:** a visible first scene with headline, action, and a living AI/OS object.
  - **Intro-to-desktop handoff:** the intro object and text give way to the real desktop.
  - **Tactile desktop:** after handoff, feed items, desktop icons, dock icons, and draggable windows respond physically.
- **Keep:**
  - Desktop OS metaphor, Hebrew-first copy, dock, menu bar, draggable widgets, workspace shortcut objects, activity feed, arcade as secondary object.
- **Redesign / strengthen:**
  - First viewport, opening copy, primary action, hero object, intro-to-desktop transition, mobile opening state.
- **Remove / avoid:**
  - Provisional ambient orbit/scanline/grid patch in `PersonalSite.tsx`.
  - Route/progress widgets and explanatory journey labels.
  - Motion that only adds glow, drift, or visual busyness.
  - Copying reference-site palette, typography, route art, illustration style, or cinematic photography.
- **Reduced motion:**
  - Keep instantaneous state changes and visible focus/active states.
  - Disable perpetual/nonessential animation.
  - Preserve orientation through static selected states, labels, and hierarchy.
- **Verification criteria:**
  - Desktop screenshot around 1440px and mobile screenshot around 390px.
  - `npm run build`.
  - Manual or browser-based check that workspace switching, icon dragging, feed tabs, dock navigation, and video lightbox still work.

column4:
**Lane:** redesign (T-067)
- **Intent:** A really cool, fluid loading animation that fits the studio/atelier art direction — shown on the **first** visit, and also on later loads that take a long time (e.g. the heavy 3D home GLB ~20MB, slow networks). Not a generic spinner.
- **Decision (brainstormed w/ Noam):** Concept = **""powering on the studio""**; approach = **hybrid** (2D CSS overlay during the GLB download → 3D camera ease-in payoff on ready); trigger = **threshold-gated** (~350ms) so first/slow loads show it and fast/cached refreshes skip it (no localStorage).
- **Done:** `StudioLoader.tsx` — CSS overlay reading real progress via drei `useProgress` (works outside Canvas); the stylized room's fixtures ignite with progress (crown trim → neon About/Service signs → monitor/arcade glow) + brass-mono % + ""מדליק את הסטודיו…"". On ready, overlay fades and `ModelScene` `CameraRig` eases from a pulled-back `START_POS` into `HOME` (new `revealed` signal via `StudioRoomModel onReady`). Reduced-motion = static fade. Safety timeout (12s) so a stalled/errored GLB can never trap the user. `?loader=1` force-previews; `?loader=0` disables (e2e opt-out). Verified: `npm run build`, screenshot of the overlay, `studio-loader.spec.ts` (2) + `studio-stations.spec.ts` (8) = 10/10 pass, no flake.
- **Possible polish (deferred):** ramp the Blender light rig 0→1 synced to the reveal (skipped to avoid per-frame React re-renders at the critical moment); first-visit-only richer variant if ever wanted.
""}

column3: **Status:** TODO (reported 2026-06-30)
column4:
**Lane:** studio
- **Symptom:** After several zoom-in/zoom-out cycles on `npm run dev`, the zoom in/out **animations stop working** — the camera no longer animates into/out of stations.
- **Likely cause:** ties to HANDOFF **#14 GL context-loss** (""depth-stencil storm"" crashing the WebGL context), or a `CameraRig` tween / open↔close state that gets stuck or accumulates across cycles. Files: `src/pages/design/studio/ModelScene.tsx`, `index.tsx`.
- **Repro:** open a station → Back → repeat ~several times → zoom stops animating. **Verify the fix on the real GPU.**
- **Acceptance:** repeated open/close cycles keep animating smoothly indefinitely; no WebGL context loss in console.
- **Investigated (2026-07-06, real GPU, headed):** drove 15 about-station cycles + 20 skills-station
  cycles via `__studioSelect` with `?gldebug=1` — **could not reproduce**: steady ~60fps every cycle,
  `__glStats` shows 0 context-lost, 0 GL errors, flat JS heap. Two apparent failures in earlier runs
  (tab ""closed"" mid-run; rAF frozen at a fixed frame count) are consistent with the automation window
  being closed/occluded on the live desktop, not an app fault. Note `ContextLossGuard`
  (`ModelScene.tsx` ~1192) already makes context loss recoverable. **Next time it happens for real:**
  reload with `?gldebug=1`, reproduce, then paste `window.__glStats` + any `[GLDIAG]` console lines —
  that pins whether it's context loss, a GL error storm, or a stuck tween.
""}

column3:
**Status:** DONE (2026-06-14)
- **Branch:** `personal-desktop-icon-system-pr-safe` (local-only until visually approved; never push to main)
- **Files:** `src/pages/design/studio/` (`index.tsx` shell+stations+panel, `Scene.tsx` camera/lights/hotspots, `furniture.tsx` low-poly room), `src/App.tsx` (dev route `/design/home-journey`), `scripts/generate-studio-scene.mjs`, `public/images/personal/journey/` (KIE renders, fallback/reference)
- **Intent:** The interactive studio-room homepage concept is approved. Current state: real Three.js low-poly room (r3f v8 + drei v9 + postprocessing, React 18 — do NOT upgrade to fiber v9), 6 hotspot stations with camera flights + in-scene OS panels, 61fps idle and during flights, three.js only in the lazy route chunk. Noam wants Polygon-Runway-level realism (reference image shared 2026-06-12).
- **Decision (2026-06-12, user-confirmed):** Path = **Blender bake pipeline**: model the room in Blender via the user's Blender MCP, bake Cycles lighting to textures, export GLTF. Mood = **night, render-quality** (twilight/lamp-light identity with soft GI, NOT the reference's daylight).
- **Pivot (2026-06-13, user-confirmed via references):** References (`docs/references/refrence_*.jpg`) revealed the target is a **fixed-angle isometric cutaway diorama** (Polygon-Runway style), not a free-orbit perspective room. Since the angle is fixed, the live Three.js `Scene.tsx` was replaced with **render + hotspots** (Option A): the Cycles render is the hero image, six absolute-positioned hotspots open the station panels. Performant (no WebGL), looks exactly like the render.
- **Done (2026-06-13):** Built the night-studio diorama in `blender/studio-room.blend` (MCP, screenshot-iterated) matching the references — iso ortho camera, cozy proportions, PolyHaven wood floor + furniture + fabric, night lighting (warm lamp pools / cool screen+window glow), full prop set (clock, framed art, plants, slat accent wall, books, rug). Rendered transparent-bg hero → `public/images/personal/journey/studio-night.png`. Rewrote `src/pages/design/studio/index.tsx` to image-diorama + 6 station hotspots (Three.js `Scene.tsx`/`furniture.tsx` no longer imported). `npm run build` passes; browser-verified idle + panel-open at `/design/home-journey`. GLB also exported (`public/models/studio-room.glb`, 15MB, unbaked — kept for the optional live-3D path, not used by the route).
- **Done (2026-06-14):** Rebuilt the current Blender source around the desk + curved monitor checkpoint: monitor base sits on the desk, rear mount/arm/neck are physically connected, the monitor screen uses the aurora cover image with aspect-preserving crop UVs (not stretched), and the saved fallback/GLB were regenerated (`public/images/personal/journey/studio-night.png`, `public/models/studio-room.glb`). Imported the Blender visual-verification guard into project-local Codex hooks and added a regression script so future Blender changes require multi-angle visual inspection before stopping.
- **Follow-ups:** (1) Fine-tune the six hotspot `pos` percentages so dots sit exactly on objects. (2) Optional realism polish in Blender (less-boxy chair, fuller plants, warmer GI) → re-render. (3) Mobile: the diorama scales but verify hotspot reachability; `.st-launcher` grid is the mobile fallback. (4) Screenshot-verify every pass — never claim done without screenshots.
- **History:** static dark prototypes → rejected; GSAP scroll journey → rejected (long/empty/flat ending); KIE 2D render room → concept approved but laggy/antique; current Three.js room → approved foundation, realism bar raised. Details in memory file `journey-homepage-direction.md`.
- **Gotchas:** `rtl-text.tsx` needed `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` because fiber augments global JSX types; site has global `scroll-behavior: smooth` (use `behavior:'instant'` in Playwright scrolls); R3F synthetic clicks need pointerdown/up before click.
""}

column3: **Status:** DESCOPED from launch (2026-06-30 — Noam confirms current real-time lighting works; the full atlas-bake pipeline is a post-launch *richness* enhancement, not a blocker. Pipeline already proven end-to-end on one wall if revisited.)
column4:
**Lane:** power-on
- **Intent:** The web reads flat/dark vs the Blender (EEVEE/Cycles) render because three.js has no GI/light bounce. Bake Cycles **indirect-only** GI lightmaps and apply them in three.js to bring the bounced richness (window/cove colour bleed) to the web — without regressing the power-on intro or overexposing. (This is the active goal-hook objective.)
- **Approach (research-confirmed):** Cycles **Diffuse bake, Color OFF, Indirect-only** (keep the existing point-light rig for direct → no double-lighting, power-on ramp still works). **Emissive zeroed during bake** so neon/screens don't smear onto walls (their light's colour bleed is still captured). One **~2k atlas** via a 2nd UV (Smart UV Project + Pack Islands). Web: load the atlas as a **separate texture** (glTF has no lightmap slot), assign `material.lightMap` by mesh name, `texture.channel=1` (uv1), `colorSpace=LinearSRGB`, **ramp `lightMapIntensity` 0→~1.2** on power-on. Floor stays the `MeshReflectorMaterial` (skip it). Watch: `gltf-transform optimize` must preserve uv1 (TEXCOORD_1).
- **Stages:** (0) validation back-wall bake → DONE. (0.5) **END-TO-END PIPELINE PROVEN on real GPU** → DONE: baked `lm_wall_back.png`, exported with uv1 referenced, optimized with `--prune-attributes false`, applied as `material.lightMap` (channel 1) on Wall_back; cranking `lightMapIntensity` visibly shows the baked window-blue bounce on the web. (1) walls + ceiling-trim **atlas** (Smart UV + Pack Islands), indirect bake (emission off), wire + `lightMapIntensity` ramp. (2) big props (bookshelf/desk/sofa/arcade). (3) intensity tune + final optimize.
- **Query A RESOLVED (was make-or-break):** `gltf-transform optimize` **prune** deletes unreferenced UV sets → the lightmap uv1 (TEXCOORD_1) was dropped. **Fix: add `--prune-attributes false`** to the optimize command → uv1 survives the full pipeline (quantized + dequantized via KHR_mesh_quantization). Also: Blender only exports the 2nd UV if a material node references it (UVMap→ImageTexture). Captured in the `r3f-blender-webgl` skill.
- **Open queries (the ""how"", not blocking):** (B) bpy workflow to bake many objects into one shared atlas; (C) Cycles indirect-only-excluding-emission exact bake setup.
- **Acceptance:** real GPU shows baked GI bounce on walls/props (visibly closes the flat/dark gap), power-on still works (black start → reveal), nothing blown out, uv1 survives export, atlas loads + ramps — judged up close, not from far crops.
""}"

**Goal:** Move spam phrases and scoring rules out of hard-coded regex lists into a reviewed config layer that can be tuned for Hebrew/Israeli spam without code edits.

**Current proof:**
- Test group `spam-test` detects Hebrew finance spam.
- LID sender spam is deduped across `message.any` and `message`.
- Delete and removal are proven in the test group.
- Rule phrases now live in `config/spam-rules.json` with tests for expanded Hebrew spam families and legitimate design/business context.

**Implementation slices:**
1. ~~Create a `config/spam-rules.json` or equivalent local config.~~
2. Split rules into severity levels:
   - high confidence: finance keyword plus link, Telegram signal redirects, wallet addresses;
   - medium confidence: finance keyword only, suspicious short pitches, media-only from new members;
   - new-member strict rules: any link during the first configured window.
3. ~~Add Hebrew phrase families:~~

{""kind"": ""source-section"", ""path"": ""/media/endlessblink/data/my-projects/ai-development/bots+automation/bina-meatezvet-bot/docs/MASTER_PLAN.md"", ""line"": 142, ""endLine"": 187, ""text"": ""### TASK-010 - Real Group Rollout Checklist

**Goal:** Safely introduce the bot into a real group with users.

**Checklist:**
1. Start detect-only:
   - `AUTO_DELETE_SPAM_MESSAGES=false`;
   - `AUTO_REMOVE_SPAMMERS=false`;
   - `AUTO_LOCK_GROUP_ON_SPAM=false`.
2. Observe detections for at least one active day.
3. Enable delete-only after false positives are reviewed.
4. Enable removals only after delete is proven and bot admin status is confirmed.
5. Keep panic lock disabled until high-volume spam behavior is observed.
6. Add rollback command and current env snapshot to the runbook.

**Progress (2026-06-25):** Custom Beer Node (`120363271484974874@g.us`, 295 members) added to live
`MODERATED_GROUPS` (now 3 groups). Started with delete+remove ON (enforce-immediately, detect-only
phase skipped by operator choice); bot confirmed admin in the group. Added reproducible deploy path
`deploy/run-bina-live.sh` + gitignored env snapshot `deploy/bina-live.env` (covers checklist item 6).
Recognition verified via synthetic benign webhook (`spam:""allow""` vs `group_not_moderated` control).
Still open: observe real detections, confirm no false positives.

**Safety layers (2026-06-25):** added admin/operator/bot/`EXEMPT_SENDERS` exemption + fail-safe so
the bot never deletes/removes trusted senders (it was removing the group owner). LID-masked groups
handled by resolving `@lid` senders to phone via WAHA `/lids/{lid}` (`src/lidCache.js`), matched
against group admins (`src/adminCache.js`) and operators; unresolvable `@lid` fails safe. Classifier
hardened: destructive action now needs a wallet, ≥2 finance keywords + link, a redirect/shortener
link, or a new member + link — a single keyword + normal link is review-only. Spec:
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-25-spam-moderation-safety-layers-design.md`. Tests 70/70.
Known gap: WEBJS engine can't reliably delete others' messages for-everyone (removal works,
deletion often doesn't) — tracked for a GOWS/NOWEB engine swap.

**Observability (2026-06-26):** WEBJS engine swap evaluated and **rejected** — deletion is actually
working when the bot is admin (8/8 deletes succeeded). Instead added: (1) **post-delete verification**
— re-list the chat after a delete and flag `spam_message_delete_unverified` + notify admins if the
message is still present (`verifySpamMessageDeleted` / `messageStillPresent`, `DELETE_VERIFY_DELAY_MS`);
(2) **full message content in admin DMs** (detection/action/failure) with a no-text placeholder, cap
raised 300→1000 (`detectionContentLine`). Tests 76/76.

**Spam tuning (2026-06-28):** real spammer slipped through as `review` — a `chat.whatsapp.com`
investment-community invite with only one matched finance keyword (single-keyword+link = review by
the false-positive guard). Fix: added `chat.whatsapp.com` to `redirectLinkPatterns` so foreign
WhatsApp group-invite links → `delete_and_remove` regardless of keyword count (like `t.me`), without
affecting normal article links. Tests 78/78. The lingering spammer (`972567267661`) was removed
manually; its old message wouldn't delete (WEBJS can't resolve a removed sender's message).
""}

**Goal:** Catch spam whose *format* the regex rules can't anticipate (novel phrasing, subtle
recruitment, invite-free promos) without raising false positives on real members.

**Design (rules-first, LLM-last):**
1. Rules + behavioral signals run first and stay the source of truth for auto-removal
   (invite link, wallet, finance+link, established-member gate). Clear spam is removed, clear
   chatter allowed — before any LLM call.
2. Only messages the rules land on `review` (the ambiguous middle) are sent to the LLM. This bounds
   volume to a handful/day, so cost/latency stay negligible.
3. LLM input = message body + light context (sender established? has link? new member?). Output =
   strict JSON `{verdict: spam
column3:
ham, confidence, reason}`.
4. **Phase 1 the LLM may only escalate to `review` or downgrade to allow — never auto-kick alone.**
   Once measured on real traffic, allow `LLM spam + a behavioral signal` to auto-remove.
5. Provider is a config switch with a timeout that fails open to the rule verdict:
   - **OpenRouter** (recommended): a cheap capable model (Gemini Flash / GPT-4o-mini / Haiku) —
     pennies/month at this volume, strong Hebrew, best for the ""hard to guess"" cases.
   - **Ollama local** (fallback): zero-cost/private; needs a 7–9B model (Qwen2.5, Gemma2) for usable
     Hebrew — a 3B is too weak for the subtle cases this is meant to catch.
6. Safety: message fed as data only (no instruction-following on user text); no auto-action on LLM
   verdict alone in phase 1.

**Validate before wiring live:** replay the logged ambiguous + known-spam messages through the
candidate model, measure catch-rate vs false-positives. Local validation via Ollama is allowed;
cloud validation runs only with explicit approval.

{""kind"": ""source-section"", ""path"": ""/media/endlessblink/data/my-projects/ai-development/bots+automation/bina-meatezvet-bot/docs/MASTER_PLAN.md"", ""line"": 280, ""endLine"": 307, ""text"": ""## TASK-012 - Uptime Watchdog & Session Resilience

**Motivation (the 2026-07-14 silent outage):** WAHA's WEBJS browser crashed (`TargetCloseError:
Target closed`); the session API still reported `WORKING` and the bot container stayed `healthy`
(HTTP 200), but zero webhooks were delivered for ~24h and ~3 spam messages slipped through with **no
alert**. Root lesson: liveness must be measured by *activity and real probes*, not by status flags,
and alerts must be *out-of-band* (a WhatsApp alert is useless when WhatsApp is what's down).

**Watchdog (external to the bot, e.g. host cron/systemd every ~5 min):**
1. Probe bot `/health`.
2. **Actively probe the session**, don't trust `WORKING`: call a WAHA endpoint that touches the
   browser (fetch 1 message) and treat a 500 / `Target closed` as DOWN.
3. **Silence detection:** alert if the bot has recorded no inbound event within N minutes during
   active hours.
4. **Dead-man's-switch:** each healthy run pings an external monitor (e.g. healthchecks.io); if the
   pings stop, the monitor notifies you — this is what *guarantees* you're told even if the whole
   host dies, because it is absence-based and off-box.
5. **Out-of-band alert channel** independent of WhatsApp: email (gws), Telegram, or ntfy/push.
6. **Self-heal:** on `Target closed`, auto-restart the `default` session with backoff + a capped
   attempt count, and alert (this is the manual fix applied on 2026-07-14).

**Resilience hardening:**
- Docker `HEALTHCHECK` should reflect reality (session truly working + a recent webhook), so the
  container stops reporting `healthy` while dead.
- Handle `session.status` transitions the bot already subscribes to (log + alert on FAILED/STOPPED)
  — but do NOT rely on it alone, since this crash emitted no status change.
- Keep `--restart unless-stopped` (already set). NOTE 2026-10-10: live container set to restart `no` while paused (WhatsApp logged out since 2026-08-07); restore on resume.
- 2026-10-10 (BUG-013): repeated `session.status` webhooks are now stored only on change; history capped; Telegram outage alert after 10 min down, repeated every 24h, with a recovery notice. Needs `OUTAGE_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` / `OUTAGE_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` set in the run script before resume.""}

**Status**: ✅ DONE (2026-01-28)

**Problem**: In local development, when user has two browser tabs open:

1. Sign in on first tab - works
2. Open second tab and try to sign in
3. Both tabs get signed out

**Symptoms**: Auth session not persisting across multiple browser tab instances during local development.

**Likely Causes**:

1. Session token overwrite/conflict between tabs
2. `onAuthStateChange` listener firing logout event to all tabs
3. Supabase local storage key collision
4. Race condition in auth initialization across tabs

**Problem**: Right-clicking on a task in the canvas inbox behaves as if Ctrl+Click was pressed (multi-select behavior) instead of opening a context menu or doing nothing.

**Root Cause**: The native `@click` event fires for ALL mouse buttons (left=0, right=2). When right-clicking, `@click` fires first (running selection logic), then `@contextmenu` fires. Canvas nodes don't have this issue because Vue Flow's `@node-click` filters by button internally.

column2:
**Status**: ✅ DONE (2026-03-13)

**Problem**: Tasks in the Mobile Today View all showed ""2:00 AM"" even though the user never set any due time. Additionally, the time-based grouping broke — all untimed tasks landed in ""Evening"" instead of ""Anytime Today"".

**Root Cause**: `MobileTodayView.vue` extracted time from `dueDate` (a date-only field) instead of checking the explicit `dueTime` field. Date-only strings like ""2026-02-08"" are parsed by `new Date()` as UTC midnight, which becomes 2:00 AM in Israel (UTC+2). The untimed task filter used `getHours() === 0` which only works in UTC+0 and fails in other timezones.

**Fix Applied (2026-02-08)**:

1. **Changed `getTaskHour()`** — Now uses `task.dueTime` instead of parsing time from `dueDate`
2. **Fixed untimed task filter** — Changed from `getHours() === 0` to `getTaskHour() === null`, making it timezone-agnostic
3. **Replaced `formatDueTime()`** — Now uses `getDueBadge()` which only shows time when explicit `dueTime` is set
4. **Fixed `sanitizeTimestamp()` in supabaseMappers.ts** — Preserves date-only strings (YYYY-MM-DD) instead of converting to UTC ISO

**Files Changed**:

- `src/mobile/views/MobileTodayView.vue` — Display and grouping fixes
- `src/utils/supabaseMappers.ts` — Preserve date-only strings

**Test Case**: Create a task with due date ""2026-02-08"" but no due time. In Israel (UTC+2), it should show ""Anytime Today"", not ""2:00 AM"".

column2:
**Status**: ✅ DONE (2026-03-13)

**Problem**: Despite BUG-1296 fix (`_rawTasks` → `rawTasks`), time block notifications are still not firing. User has a 120-min calendar block scheduled and received no milestone alerts (halfway, 1-min-before, ended).

**Root Causes Found** (multi-agent investigation):

1. **Late tolerance too tight** (2 min) — desktop apps sleep/background, `setInterval` skips ticks, milestones silently missed
2. **Singleton guard fragile** — module-level `isInitialized` survives but interval could die, `start()` refuses to restart
3. **Silent notification delivery** — `deliverNotification()` had no error handling, no logging, failed invisibly
4. **Missing permission request** — Timer store requests Notification permission at init, but time blocks didn't
5. **Instance data not in sync queue** — `createTaskInstance` was fire-and-forget, instances not backed up by sync queue
6. **Toast too short** — 5s duration easy to miss

**Fixes Applied** (4 files):

1. `useTimeBlockNotifications.ts` — Late tolerance 2min→10min, resilient singleton (restarts if interval died), delivery logging, toast duration 5s→8s, skip completed/soft-deleted tasks
2. `notificationDelivery.ts` — Added try-catch, logging on permission denied/API unavailable/delivery success, returns boolean
3. `useAppInitialization.ts` — Explicit `Notification.requestPermission()` before starting time block polling
4. `taskOperations.ts` — Added `instances` to sync queue payload for offline backup

**Files**:

- `src/composables/useTimeBlockNotifications.ts` — Core composable (polling, milestone detection, delivery)
- `src/utils/notificationDelivery.ts` — Browser Notification API wrapper
- `src/composables/app/useAppInitialization.ts` — Where composable is mounted
- `src/stores/tasks/taskOperations.ts` — Sync queue payload for instance persistence

**Status**: ✅ DONE (2026-03-13)

**Problem**: In the calendar week view, events on Monday and Tuesday render correctly with proper width, title, time, and duration. However, events on Thursday through Sunday appear as nearly invisible thin vertical lines/slivers instead of proper event blocks.

**Root Cause**: CSS `.week-event { left: var(--space-1); right: var(--space-1); }` overrode the JS-computed percentage-based `left`/`width` from `getWeekEventStyle()`. The fixed CSS values clamped all events to the same position regardless of day column.

**Fix Applied**:

- [x] Removed CSS `left`/`right` overrides from `.week-event` in `CalendarWeekView.vue`
- [x] Added 2px inset padding via `calc()` in `getWeekEventStyle()` for column gap

**Files Changed**:

- `src/components/calendar/CalendarWeekView.vue` — Removed conflicting CSS left/right
- `src/composables/calendar/useCalendarWeekView.ts` — `calc()` padding in left/width

column2:
**Status**: ✅ DONE (2026-03-13)

**Problem**: Production console (in-theflow.com) flooded with 5 categories of noise:

1. Hundreds of `[WakeLock] Failed to request wake lock: DOMException` when tab is hidden
2. `[SYNC] LWW: Server wins` on every sync cycle (echo from direct save + sync queue race)
3. `[SUPABASE-MAPPER] Invalid UUID detected` on every sync for legacy group ""Today""
4. `[REALTIME] Connection dropped (CHANNEL_ERROR)` when browser suspends background WebSockets
5. Transient CORS/network failures from ServiceWorker during tab sleep (handled by existing retry)

**Fix**: 4 targeted changes:

- `useWakeLock.ts`: Guard `requestWakeLock()` with `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'` check
- `useSyncOrchestrator.ts`: Downgrade LWW echo logs (delta < 2s) from `warn` to `debug`
- `supabaseMappers.ts`: Deduplicate warnings via `Set` — legacy group/UUID warnings fire once per session
- `useSupabaseDatabase.ts`: Downgrade CHANNEL_ERROR/CLOSED to `debug` when tab is hidden

**Files**: `src/composables/useWakeLock.ts`, `src/composables/sync/useSyncOrchestrator.ts`, `src/utils/supabaseMappers.ts`, `src/composables/useSupabaseDatabase.ts`
